title: Permission inventory collection (foundational)
description: The auditor collects the complete permission inventory: every role, every grant, every user-to-role assignment. Collection pulls from the live systems, not from documentation, because documentation drifts. The inventory is the ground truth for everything the auditor concludes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Access Control and Permission Auditor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Effective access computation per user (foundational)
description: Each user's effective permissions are computed as the union of all grants from all their roles, including nested role inheritance. The computation resolves the full inheritance chain so indirect grants are not missed. Effective access is what the user can actually do, regardless of what any single role suggests. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Access Control and Permission Auditor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Over-privilege detection (foundational)
description: Effective access is compared against each user's declared job needs; permissions held but never used within the review window are flagged as over-privilege. Usage comes from the access decision log, so the finding is evidence-based. Flagged grants go to managers for approval or removal, not straight to deletion. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Access Control and Permission Auditor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Segregation-of-duties check (foundational)
description: The auditor checks segregation rules, such as no single user holding both 'approve-payment' and 'issue-payment'. Violations are found by testing each user's effective access against the forbidden combinations list. Segregation failures are reported as high severity because they enable fraud, not just accidents. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
eff = {'approve-payment', 'issue-payment'}
forbidden = [{'approve-payment', 'issue-payment'}]
viol = [c for c in forbidden if c <= eff]
print('segregation violations:', viol if viol else 'none')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Access Control and Permission Auditor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Access decision log with enforcement (foundational)
description: Every access decision, allow or deny, is logged with the user, resource, action, and the rule that decided it, and denials are enforced at the boundary. The log is append-only and reviewed on a schedule. Enforcement plus logging is what turns access control from a policy document into a working boundary. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
log = []
def decide(user, action, allowed):
    log.append({'user': user, 'action': action, 'decision': 'ALLOW' if allowed else 'DENY'})
    return allowed
decide('u1', 'delete', False)
print('enforced:', log[0]['decision'], '| logged:', len(log), 'entries')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Access Control and Permission Auditor practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
